rubric_items.reason: All 8 design components (CO-1 to CO-8) appear by exact name and each has at least one threat. Changed endpoints EP-1 to EP-3 are covered through patientsRouter and PatientService.get.

Most threats fit their component: unscoped count, SQL injection on the id, no-auth MVP, response widening on POST/PATCH. T-7, T-8 and T-12 are correctness or regression risks labelled as STRIDE tampering.

Each mitigation is either cited (C1-C13) or named as a new control for implement, with tests (S-1 AC5, S-3 AC1/AC2). T-6 has no real control, only an accepted MVP risk, and it cites patients:read although POST/PATCH use patients:write.
The no-sign-in gap is stated openly in T-6 and T-10. But the text calls it an 'accepted MVP risk' without citing who accepted it, and assumed, unknown and questions are all empty.
Readable, and the frontmatter and body match one to one. Threats follow component order rather than risk, so the highest-risk items (no auth, T-6/T-10) come after lower-risk type-drift items.

findings.text: T-5 says the create and update responses also expose the counts, but T-6's mitigation cites only patients:read (C3). POST and PATCH are gated by patients:write, so T-6's permission control does not describe those paths.

cites.quote: the route declares patients:read through requirePermission (C2, C3)
the create and update responses built by the same get (C12)
requirePermission('patients:write')

findings.suggested_fix: In T-6, name both permissions: patients:read for GET /:id and patients:write for POST and PATCH, which also return visitSummary.

findings.text: T-6 calls the risk an 'accepted MVP risk', but no context section or answer records that acceptance. The architecture section only says every permission is granted in the MVP.

cites.quote: accepted MVP risk, unchanged by HMS-5
In the MVP every request is the actor `staff` and every permission is granted.

findings.suggested_fix: Say the risk is inherited and unchanged by HMS-5, or cite where it was accepted. Otherwise list it as Assumed.

findings.text: Threats are listed by component, not by risk. The no-authentication threats (T-6, T-10) sit after lower-impact type-drift threats (T-7, T-8).

cites.quote: T-10 (patientsRouter, spoofing): there is no sign-in in the MVP.
T-8 (Web type PatientDetail, tampering): the web and API types drift apart.

findings.suggested_fix: Order the Threats section by risk, or add a risk rank to each threat.

findings.text: T-7, T-8 and T-12 are functional or regression defects (text counts, type drift, table changed by mistake) with no adversary. Labelling them STRIDE tampering overstates them as security threats.

Changes for the Visit summary alter the appointments list

findings.suggested_fix: Mark these as integrity or correctness risks, or move them to a non-STRIDE note, so the security threats stand out.
